title: The treatment API shapes, the treatment table set, the case-state reporting and the decision code of a treatment event are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E3-001 sections 1 to 19 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md lines 975 to 1072); FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.1; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.0, T3.1 and T-A.1 to T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 41, 42 and 43; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 18; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 and R7.2 s12
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.5; 12.7; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the treatment resource. (1) TSD T-A.1 and T-A.2 name four treatment paths and the entity names TreatmentRequest, TreatmentUpdate and Treatment with no field list for any of them, so the request and response elements of POST /cases/{caseId}/treatments and GET /treatments/{treatmentId} are named but their contents are not. (2) TSD T3.1 gives the treatment fields DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 but no table or field list for the contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements and plan timers that Architecture v5 slide 41 places in the rwb_treatment schema. (3) No source states how a stage workflow reports its outcome to the case or who moves the case status: the legacy story moved recovery_case.status in one schema, and the target gives the case and its CMMN state to rwb-case. (4) No source fixes the decision code a treatment event carries to the decision-record library, although every acceptance criterion ends with the record being written with the rule version. (5) The access right of each operation is named by capability area and right only, and the roles of TSD T6.1 list fourteen human roles and three system identities without stating which right each of the new elements needs.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T-A.1 (API-S2-001 POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/treatments, API-S2-002 GET /api/recovery/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}, API-S2-003 PATCH, API-S2-004 POST /submit) and T-A.2 (Request TreatmentRequest, Response Treatment, Errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503) with no field table; TSD S2 v2 T3.1 starts at DF-TRT-001 and ends at DF-TRT-033 for treatment only; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 ('S2 | rwb-treatment | treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements, plan timers | rwb_treatment | /treatments | rwb.treatment.events.v1 | rwb-treatment | 2') and slide 18 ('DB writes schema rwb_treatment: treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements, plan timers'); legacy RWB-E3-001 section 4 ('Then open the treatment record and ask COLLINS for the restructure proposal') and section 11 data table naming recovery_case, treatment, decision_log_entry and rule_row; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12 (tables 12.1 to 12.9) and R5.5 DP-03
area: Contract and data: treatment shapes, table set, case-state reporting, decision code
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-treatment with the P3 owner of the case contract and the owner of the local decision-record library
proposed: Publish the working read of ASM-B-S2-01-E3001-1 with RWB-S2-E3001-CON and apply it to RWB-S2-E3001-APP: the Treatment and TreatmentRequest elements named in camelCase after DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033, treatment as the only table this story creates, the other four objects with the sibling stories that own them, the stage outcome reported to the parent CaseWorkflow which owns and moves the case status, and the decision code taken from the evaluated package. Confirm with the P3 owner of the case contract at the wave 2 contract freeze.

title: The settlement offer operation, its body and the range and floor facts are not specified for rwb-treatment
source: Legacy RWB-E3-002 sections 1 to 19 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md lines 1074 to 1172); FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.2; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.1, T4 SETTLEMENT and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 41; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-04, R-RES-07, R-RES-15 and R-SET-05
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4; 8 Business rules; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.7; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the settlement offer. (1) TSD T3.1 carries no floor, no range and no validity column and defines no SettlementOffer entity, although the legacy story offers an amount inside a calculated range and warns when the payoff is stale. (2) The FSD says the range and the floor come from the payoff and range calculation of another module and that an offer below the floor needs approval, without naming the fields that carry the range, the floor or the gap to the floor. (3) API Specification v4 and TSD T-A.1 name no offer-specific operation at all; the legacy story's own endpoint table lists only the treatment create and read, so the write that builds the offer is published nowhere. (4) No source states whether the range and the floor are stored on the treatment, read at request time, or carried on the route decision signal, and storing them would copy another service's facts into rwb_treatment.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (treatment fields DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033, none of them a floor, a range or a below-floor flag) and T-A.1 (API-S2-001 to API-S2-004, none of them an offer); legacy RWB-E3-002 section 7 ('Then lets the officer build and send a settlement offer within the calculated range') and section 14 (MSG-S2-001 'The offer is below the floor of {floor}.', MSG-S2-002 'The payoff is from {date}.', MSG-S2-003 'The offer to the customer ends on {date}.'); FSD S2 v3 A2.2.3.1 (R-RES-07, R-RES-04, R-RES-15) and A1.1 Dependencies (FEAT-VAL-06); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18 ('REST GET/POST /treatments - POST /treatments/{id}/offer') and slide 41 (rwb-treatment owns treatments and settlement agreements); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-SET-05 ('offer_amount < floor_price' moves to AWAITING_APPROVAL_SET)
area: Contract and data: settlement offer body, range and floor facts
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-treatment with the S1 owner of the payoff and range calculation
proposed: Publish the working read of ASM-B-S2-01-E3002-1 in RWB-S2-E3002-CON and apply it to RWB-S2-E3002-APP: the offer body carries offerAmount, haircutAmount, validityDate, rangeLow, rangeHigh, floor and deviationFlag and the answer carries belowFloor, the range and the floor arrive as facts on the route decision signal from rwb-case and no range, floor or validity column is created in rwb_treatment. Confirm with the S1 owner of FEAT-VAL-06 at the wave 2 contract freeze.

title: The offer operation is /treatments/{id}/offer in Architecture v5 and /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit in API Specification v4 and the TSD
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18 (rwb-treatment IN); Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 x-module S2; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T-A.1 API-S2-004; Template and Rules v1 R3 source precedence
section: 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1; 12.1; 19 Out of scope
description: A conflict of paths. Architecture v5 slide 18 names POST /treatments/{id}/offer as the rwb-treatment IN operation, while API Specification v4 (x-module S2) and TSD S2 T-A.1 API-S2-004 name POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit for the same purpose, submitting a treatment for approval. Template and Rules R3 puts the Architecture v5 catalogue slides above the Technical Specifications and the Functional Specifications, so the target may publish only one of the two forms, and the other has to be recorded as superseded so that no caller builds against a path that will not exist.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18 notes ('rwb-treatment (S2, TDR, settlement, DIL) IN: REST GET/POST /treatments; POST /treatments/{id}/offer'); TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T-A.1 row API-S2-004 ('POST | /api/recovery/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}/submit | Treatment and offer U | E3') and T-A.2 ('Purpose | Submit a treatment for approval'); Template and Rules v1 R3 item 1 (Arch v5 catalogue slides 13 to 20 and 41 to 44) above item 6 (Technical Specifications by Module)
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-treatment tech lead
proposed: Publish one operation, POST /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}/offer, carrying the submit semantics of API-S2-004, and record /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit as superseded in the contract change note and in the change register. Confirm with the solution architect at the wave 2 contract freeze.

title: The below-floor approval record, the delegation facts, the reason code and the TreatmentApproved payload are not specified for rwb-treatment
source: Legacy RWB-E3-003 sections 1 to 19 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md lines 1175 to 1272); FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.3; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.1, T4 DEEDINLIEU and T4 SETTLEMENT; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 41 and 42; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 6 and 18; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIL-15, R-DIL-17 and R-SET-05; Ownership Map row delegation_limit
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4; 8 Business rules; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.3; 12.7; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the below-floor path. (1) TSD T3.1 has no second-signature field, no approver reference and no approval-outcome record beyond approval_level, although the legacy story routes the price to an approver or a committee named in the matrix and records the refusal with a reason. (2) The delegation facts live in rwb-access's delegation_limit table and no source states how rwb-treatment reads them for an approval request or which level a below-floor settlement takes. (3) No source lists the reason codes; price_below_floor appears once, in the rule row R-DIL-17. (4) Architecture v5 slide 42 gives TreatmentApproved with its producer rwb-treatment and its consumers rwb-comms and rwb-payment but no payload, key or envelope, and Template and Rules R4 fixes only the topic and the event name.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (treatment fields DF-TRT-011 approval_level only) and T4 DEEDINLIEU rows R-DIL-15 ('TRANSFER_PRICE_SET | PRICE_BELOW_FLOOR | AWAITING_SECOND_SIGNATURE') and R-DIL-17 ('AWAITING_SECOND_SIGNATURE | SECOND_SIGNATURE_REFUSED | RETURNED_TO_ROUTE_DIL'); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIL-15 ('Head of NPA') and R-DIL-17 ('reason price_below_floor'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 row 10 ('10 | TreatmentApproved | rwb-treatment | rwb.treatment.events.v1 | rwb-comms, rwb-payment') and slide 18 ('TMP Decision: child: approval'); Ownership Map row delegation_limit (owner P4, 'The DoA table is P4 rwb-access'); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 6 (settlement approval limits are versioned and take effect on a date) and slide 18 ('Settlement below floor -> approval (R-SET-05)', 'Deed below floor: Head of NPA (R-DIL-15)')
area: Contract and data: approval outcome, DoA facts, reason code, event payload
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-treatment with the rwb-access owner of the DoA table and the rwb-decision owner of the approval workflow
proposed: Publish the working read of ASM-B-S2-01-E3003-1 in RWB-S2-E3003-CON and apply it to RWB-S2-E3003-APP: the approval outcome recorded on the treatment row as approval_level plus the final call, the approver role and the decided-at time with no new table, the delegation level and limit carried on the approval request of the kit's ApprovalWorkflow, price_below_floor as a reference value, and a TreatmentApproved payload of treatmentId, caseId, treatmentType, offerAmount, approvalLevel, approverRole, finalCall, decidedAt, ruleId and ruleVersion. Confirm with the rwb-access and rwb-decision owners at the wave 2 contract freeze.

title: The TDR plan body, the band and the plan write operation are not specified for rwb-treatment
source: Legacy RWB-E3-004 sections 1 to 19 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md lines 1275 to 1371); FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.4; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.1, T4 RESTRUCTURE and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 41; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-04, R-RES-07 and R-RES-15
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4; 8 Business rules; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.5; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the TDR plan. (1) TSD T3.1 carries the plan fields (installments, installment_amount, interest_rate, first_due_date, valid_until) but defines no plan entity, no band and no write operation for a plan. (2) The legacy story's endpoint table lists only GET /treatments/{treatmentId}, so its write path is published nowhere, and the FSD says the plan offer is built and sent with the band and the rule version applied without naming a shape. (3) The band is produced by the ACE affordability calculation of FEAT-TRT-05 and no source states whether the band is stored with the offer or read again at each use. (4) The offer clock is described as a timer; no source states whether it is a row in the timer table, which is rwb-case's, or a durable Temporal timer inside the stage workflow, although Architecture v5 slide 44 retires the five-minute timer check in favour of durable timers.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-009 installments, DF-TRT-027 interest_rate, DF-TRT-029 first_due_date, DF-TRT-031 installment_amount, DF-TRT-010 valid_until) and T-A.1 (no plan operation); legacy RWB-E3-004 section 7 ('Then lets the restructuring officer build and send the plan offer, with the band and the rule version applied') and its Endpoints table (only GET /api/recovery/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}); FSD S2 v3 A2.4.3.1 (R-RES-04, R-RES-07, R-RES-15) and A2.4.2 ('Integration points. COLLINS, EFS, ACE and TDR'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-05 retired, durable timers inside each workflow) and slide 18 (TreatmentWorkflow carries the plan timers); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-04 ('start the offer clock', 2 working days) and R-RES-07
area: Contract and data: plan body, band facts, plan write path, offer clock
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-treatment with the S1 owner of the valuation and the ACE affordability result
proposed: Publish the working read of ASM-B-S2-01-E3004-1 in RWB-S2-E3004-CON and apply it to RWB-S2-E3004-APP: the PlanOffer body carries installmentCount, installmentAmount, interestRate, firstDueDate, validUntil, bandLow and bandHigh, the plan terms are recorded on the treatment row, the band arrives with the affordability result and no band column is created, and the offer clock is a durable Temporal timer inside TreatmentWorkflow with no timer row written. Confirm with the S1 owner at the wave 2 contract freeze.

title: The plan write path is /treatments/{id}/offer in Architecture v5 and /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit in API Specification v4 and the TSD, and the legacy endpoint table names neither
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18 (rwb-treatment IN); Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 x-module S2; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T-A.1 API-S2-004; Legacy RWB-E3-004 Endpoints table; Template and Rules v1 R3 source precedence
section: 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1; 12.1; 19 Out of scope
description: A conflict of paths, and a gap behind it. Architecture v5 slide 18 names POST /treatments/{id}/offer; API Specification v4 and TSD S2 T-A.1 API-S2-004 name POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit; and the legacy story for this key lists only the GET, so its own write path is named by no source at all. Template and Rules R3 puts the Architecture v5 catalogue above the Technical Specifications, so one form is published and the other recorded as superseded, and the plan body has to be bound to that one operation rather than to a second path.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18 ('REST GET/POST /treatments - POST /treatments/{id}/offer'); TSD S2 v2 T-A.1 row API-S2-004 and T-A.2 ('Purpose | Submit a treatment for approval'); legacy RWB-E3-004 Endpoints table (one row, GET /api/recovery/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}); Template and Rules v1 R3 item 1 above item 6 and R7.2 s12
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-treatment tech lead
proposed: Submit the plan through POST /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}/offer with the PlanOffer body, on the one operation RWB-S2-E3002-CON declares; do not publish /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit and record it as superseded. Confirm with the solution architect at the wave 2 contract freeze.

title: The ACE Common restructure calculator binding, its result fields and its failure path are not specified for rwb-treatment
source: Legacy RWB-E3-005 sections 1 to 19 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md lines 1374 to 1468); FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.5; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.1, T4 RESTRUCTURE and T5.1 INT-34; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18 (NEXUS ACE Common: restructure calculator); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 10, 13 and 18; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-06 and R-RES-07
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4; 11 Data; 12.2; 12.5; 12.8; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the affordability step. (1) Architecture v5 slide 18 names the restructure calculator as a Nexus operation into ACE Common and gives no operation name, request or response. (2) TSD T5.1 gives INT-34 as the ACE common module with a 'published module interface' and no operation, and TSD T-A.1 lists no affordability path of any service. (3) TSD T3.1 has no affordability result field and no plan reference column, although the story records the result against the offer. (4) No source states the timeout, the retry or the answer when the calculator does not reply, and the FSD's 'ACE and TDR' integration names a system that Architecture v5 keeps outside the 19 services.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18 ('NEXUS ACE Common: restructure calculator (Nexus)'); TSD S2 v2 T5.1 row INT-34 ('ACE common module | Both | Published module interface | Per request') and T3.1 (no affordability or plan_ref field); FSD S2 v3 A2.5.2 ('Integration points. ACE and TDR') and A2.5.3.1 (R-RES-06, R-RES-07); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 10 ('ace-collection is ACE's namespace, reached through Nexus (for example the restructure calculator)') and slide 18 ('ACE affordability check | R-RES-06'); legacy RWB-E3-005 section 7 ('Then calls the ACE affordability calculation and records the result against the offer')
area: Contract: Nexus calculator binding, result fields, failure path
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-treatment with the ACE Common owner and the platform workflow owner
proposed: Publish the working read of ASM-B-S2-01-E3005-1 in RWB-S2-E3005-CON and apply it to RWB-S2-E3005-APP: one Nexus operation calculateRestructurePlan in the ace-collection namespace, request with the case ID, the plan inputs and the rule version, answer with affordabilityResult, planRef, installmentAmount, installmentCount and calculatedAt, a 2 s synchronous budget with the workflow's retry, and the stage held in AFFORDABILITY_IN_ACE with MSG-GEN-006 when the calculator does not answer. Confirm the operation with the ACE Common owner at the wave 2 contract freeze.
